summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for acute worsening of chronic diastolic heart failure, presenting with dyspnea, chest pain, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. Initial concern for ACS was ruled out with normal cardiac biomarkers and EKG showing no acute ischemia. A chest X-ray showed stable cardiomegaly without acute findings. He was treated with IV furosemide, leading to symptom improvement and weight reduction. His warfarin was held due to a supratherapeutic INR of 3.7 and later restarted at a reduced dose. Glyburide was held in favor of insulin during admission, with plans to resume at home. Eosinophilia was noted but found to be a chronic finding on review of records. He was discharged home in stable condition with increased diuretic therapy, medication adjustments, and follow-up plans including a cardiac stress test.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Heart valve replaced by other means
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
